extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting to the American Journal of Health Behavior; journal press officers and media reporters
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and rules governing embargoes on manuscript-related information for the American Journal of Health Behavior, including author and reporter obligations, exceptions, and consequences for violations. Also states the journal's adherence to the Ingelfinger Rule on prior publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: An embargo is an agreement between author(s) of scientific manuscripts, peer-reviewed journals and reporters concerning the release of information to the media in advance of a specific publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This agreement notes that the author(s) will defer releasing information and that the news media will defer coverage until a specified date set by the publisher (Am J Health Behav).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/Timing of the Embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: The embargo applies to the time between the submission of the manuscript to the publisher and the authorized release of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must defer releasing information during this period and the media must defer coverage until the publisher-authorized date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author obligation to avoid premature public statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should follow these practices when making research results public and not issue premature public statements about their work before it has been published by the Am J Health Behav.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who violate this embargo will be banned from future publication in the Am J Health Behav.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter/media obligation to honor embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: News media agree to defer coverage of embargoed information until the specified release date set by the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters who violate embargo will be excluded from future embargoed information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted interviews under embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may give interviews to representatives of the media who agree to the Am J Health Behav embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The embargo notes the information is confidential and cannot be made public by the media until you have received your final corrected PDF and there are no pending fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality condition before public release
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoed information is confidential and cannot be made public by the media until authors have received their final corrected PDF and there are no pending fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition is part of the embargo agreement and a prerequisite for authorized public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: The embargo concept is designed to assure that the information conveyed to broader audiences through these practices is accurate and fairly presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In tandem the two policies ensure that journal readers will have the full article when the media report on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of embargo violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions are applied for violating the embargo by either party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters who violate embargo will be excluded from future embargoed information. Authors who violate this embargo will be banned from future publication in the Am J Health Behav.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingelfinger Rule (no prior substantial publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Am J Health Behav considers publication of the scientific manuscript only on the condition that its key substance has not been submitted or reported elsewhere (the Ingelfinger Rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal does not wish to receive manuscripts on work that has already been presented or published in large part elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and restrictions for conference or public presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: A key exception to the Ingelfinger Rule is presenting material at scientific conferences, congressional hearings or other government proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data may have been reported at a scientific meeting; however, authors must refrain from presenting or handing out copies of author tables, figures and/or illustrations. It is also acceptable to talk to reporters in these venues; however, comments should be limited to what was addressed in the presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related copyright and deposition policies (references)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page references other policies: Copyright / Violations, Reprint & Copy Policy, PMC Deposit Process/Matrix, Need a PMCID?, Depository Policy, Depository Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These linked items indicate additional procedural and legal requirements related to publication, copyright, and repository deposit; follow those policies as applicable.
